analysis.title: Vale (VALE): 3Q26 In Line; Mine Supply & Costs A Question Into 2027
key_insights: Vale 3Q26 pro-forma EBITDA was $3,508M, in line with GS ($3,288M, +7%) and Visible Alpha consensus ($3,539M, -1%). EBITDA fell 14% q/q and 20% y/y per Exhibit 1. GS expects a neutral market reaction but says poor product mix and rising cost risk could surprise negatively.

Iron ore mine supply fell 9% y/y on Serra Norte depletion of 27% y/y in the headline (30% y/y in the detail). GS says resources look to be running down faster than expected at Vale's second-best operation. A change to the cavity decree framework may be needed to reverse the trend, which puts downside risk on the 2027 production outlook.
The open question for 2027 is whether the +20 project and Vargem Grande/Capanema can offset the Serra Norte decline.

Third-party purchases were strong in 3Q26 and partly offset the mine supply weakness. GS says this is unlikely to be sustainable in 2027 given high freight rates and a low iron ore price, which make those volumes less competitive.

Product mix keeps shifting toward lower-margin products. IOCJ (high-grade Carajas) is now under 5% of the mix, replaced by mid-grade Carajas at over 20%. 3Q26 iron ore realization was 10% lower q/q, mostly from the quality premium and an FOB sales adjustment tied to higher freight.

Iron ore fines EBITDA was $2,078M, 3% above GS but 11% below Visible Alpha consensus. Volume was in line, with a worse mix and more third-party purchases than expected. Realized price ($85/t) and cash COGS ($57/t) were close to GS estimates.

Iron ore pellets EBITDA was $516M, 19% above GS and 30% above consensus. Cash COGS of $82/t beat GS by 7%, likely from fixed-cost dilution. Pellet production is on track for the mid-point of 30-34mt guidance.

Copper EBITDA was $1,021M, flat q/q and up 66% y/y, 7% above GS and 15% above consensus. Realization reached 109% of the LME benchmark (105% in 2Q26), helped by provisional-pricing timing (a $1,300/t positive impact) and favorable TC/RCs. Sossego downtime from a SAG mill repair cost $40M (about $570/t).

Copper production fell 13% q/q and 6% y/y on the Sossego downtime, partly offset by Salobo's strongest 3Q. Vale is on track for the upper half of FY26 guidance. Reaching the 380kt high end would need 94kt in 4Q26 versus GS at 88kt. The CPF project (30ktpa of added copper) is 17% complete, with start-up expected in 1H28.

Nickel EBITDA was $98M, in line with GS (-3%) and 50% below consensus, down 67% q/q and 14% y/y. Sales were 11% above GS and price realization was 102% of LME, but cash costs of $15,212/t were 6% above GS and up 38% q/q on inventory turnover, maintenance, lower grade, energy and fuel.

Iron ore cost guidance is under pressure. 9M26 C1 is $23.6/t against a guidance range of $22.5-23.5/t, while the production guidance of 335-345mt is expected to land close to the low end. Diesel prices are rising, Brazil diesel subsidies may be lifted, and freight and bunker fuel are headwinds, partly offset by contracted volume.

Net income was $1,255M, 17% below GS and 26% below consensus. Calculated free cash flow was $1,078M versus GS at $280M, helped by operating cash flow 29% above GS and capex 13% below. Expanded net debt was $16.4B, or 1.0x LTM EBITDA.

GS stays Neutral with a 12-month price target of $14 (stock $11.18, 25.2% upside), using a 50/50 blend of DCF (WACC 9.0%, beta 1.10) and 12-month forward EV/EBITDA of 5.2x. Vale trades at a 4-6% FCF yield in 2027-28, in line with its Australian peers.

Earnings call is on October 30 at 10am EST. GS will look for detail on iron ore price and cost pressure into 4Q26 and 2027, China demand, base metals operations, capital allocation priorities, and potential negotiations with CMRG.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral kept after an in-line 3Q26. Mine supply depletion, a weaker product mix and rising costs weigh on 2027, and the 4-6% FCF yield is in line with Australian peers.

earnings_insights: Vale 3Q26 reported (pro-forma) EBITDA $3,508M vs GS estimate $3,288M and Visible Alpha consensus $3,539M. Already printed, reported 10/30/2026.
Vale 3Q26 net income $1,255M reported vs GS estimate $1,506M and consensus $1,702M. Already printed.
Vale 3Q26 net revenue $10,599M reported vs GS estimate $9,934M and consensus $10,402M. Already printed.
Iron ore fines EBITDA $2,078M reported vs GS estimate $2,019M and consensus $2,339M. Pellets EBITDA $516M reported vs GS estimate $434M and consensus $396M. Already printed.
Copper EBITDA $1,021M reported vs GS estimate $958M and consensus $885M. Nickel EBITDA $98M reported vs GS estimate $101M and consensus $197M. Already printed.

FY26 guidance as reported by management: iron ore production close to the lower end of 335-345mt, pellets near the mid-point of 30-34mt, copper and nickel in the upper half of range. GS sees C1/t guidance pressured, with 9M26 at $23.6/t vs a $22.5-23.5/t range.
GS forecasts (not reported): 2026E EPS $1.67, 2027E $1.45, 2028E $1.53. Quarterly EPS estimates are $0.35 for 3Q26E, $0.32 for 4Q26E and $0.36 for 1Q27E, against $0.32 reported for 2Q26.
risk_factors: Downside: a China macro slowdown that cuts iron ore prices.
Downside: a stronger BRL versus USD.
Downside: weaker copper and nickel supply and demand dynamics that push base metals lower.
Downside: further legal actions on Samarco that could raise provisions.
Downside: operational misses in iron ore or base metals that lower volumes and cash flow.

Upside: stronger China steel demand from a property or infrastructure rebound, supply disruptions or slower new iron ore capacity ramp-up, faster electrification and grid spending that lifts copper, and a stronger USD versus BRL.
Serra Norte depletion running faster than expected, with a possible cavity decree change not in place in time.
Rising diesel costs, a possible end to Brazil diesel subsidies, and high freight and bunker fuel costs.

tension_points.bull_case: The +20 project and Vargem Grande/Capanema could offset Serra Norte depletion, and a cavity decree framework change could reverse the decline. Management is confident of delivering FY26 production guidance.
tension_points.bear_case: Serra Norte depletion is running at -27% to -30% y/y, mine supply fell 9% y/y, and third-party purchases that covered the gap lose profitability at a low iron ore price and high freight. Mix is shifting to lower-margin products and diesel and freight costs are rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A change to the cavity decree framework that is effectively implemented, or evidence on the earnings call that the Serra Norte decline is largely reversible.

theme_stances.key_argument: Serra Norte depletion is accelerating and is hard to offset before a cavity decree change is implemented, which puts 2027 production at risk.
theme_stances.evidence: resources are being exhausted faster than expected in the second best Vale operation

theme_stances.key_argument: Diesel, freight and a lower-margin product mix should weigh on 2027 margins and price realization.
theme_stances.evidence: Vale c1 cost has been under pressure due to rising diesel prices
